title: editcap: Add extract-secrets
description:
Add an extract-secrets option to editcap, to write the information from
DSBs back to file(s). It takes over the output file and ignores all
other options. If there are multiple DSBs, each is written to a
separate file (some types could be concatenated possibly, but not all.)

Document and add a test.

Fix #18197

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 5d4115aa - editcap: Add extract-secrets
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16392/diffs?diff_id=1062495830&start_sha=5ffbaa8087f03f3a7a96ecead4e824fc9b39911c)

> It takes over the output file and ignores all other options.

Should it ignore them, or should it either 1) warn about if an option that doesn't apply is supplied or 2) fail if an option that doesn't apply is supplied?  That might reduce the chances of a bug being filed complaining that Wireshark is ignoring some option when `--extract-secrets` is used.
Sure, couldn't hurt to warn or fail, because even with help messages and man pages, people complain. I'll implement that.

++
+--
+Extracts each Decryption Secrets Block (DSB) contained within __infile__.

+If there is more than one, they are each written to unique output files named

+    def test_pcapng_dsb_extract(self, cmd_editcap, dirs, capture_file, result_file, check_pcapng_dsb_fields, base_env):
+        '''Check that extracted DSBs match the original key log files.'''
+        dsb_keys1 = os.path.join(dirs.key_dir, 'tls12-dsb-1.keys')
+        dsb_keys2 = os.path.join(dirs.key_dir, 'tls12-dsb-2.keys')
+        outfile = result_file('tls12-dsb-extract.key')
+        subprocess.run((cmd_editcap,
+            '--extract-secrets',
+            capture_file('tls12-dsb.pcapng'), outfile
+        ), check=True, env=base_env)
+        p = PurePath(outfile)
+        with open(dsb_keys1, 'r') as f:
+            dsb1_contents = f.read().encode('utf8')
+        with open(dsb_keys2, 'r') as f:
+            dsb2_contents = f.read().encode('utf8')
+        # Python 3.9 and higher has p.with_stem(p.stem + "_00000"))
+        with open(p.with_name(p.stem + "_00000" + p.suffix)) as f:
+            dsb1_out = f.read().encode('utf8')
+        with open(p.with_name(p.stem + "_00001" + p.suffix)) as f:
+            dsb2_out = f.read().encode('utf8')
+        assert dsb1_contents == dsb1_out
+        assert dsb2_contents == dsb2_out
